notes: scan060.N1: The page continues the discussion of neighbourhood germs/topoi, introduces a three-index neighbourhood in (10), defines S_{j,k} in (11), then writes two classes of indices and the formulas (12). It records endpoint equalities (13) and a tentative expectation of a locally trivial bundle over X_i^*, allowing a singular fibre. The last sentence is unfinished. The page is handwritten text, with a right-margin NB and pale other-hand foliation 59; there is no dark authorial number at the head.

scan060.N2: Literal mathematical notation is not repaired. The live first R index in (10) is i, above a crossed j-like form; the first R index in (12) is a descending j. The first set label has a star before (k)', whereas the first union bound in (12) uses I^{(k)'} without a star. The right-hand intersection assertion in (12) ends in dotted X_i, not dotted X_j. scan060.N3: Targeted elementary partition check. Let J be whichever index set the doubtful I^(k) definition denotes, and put P={ell in J: X_ell does not contain X_j}, Q={ell in J: X_ell contains X_j}. Every ell in J satisfies exactly one of the condition and its negation, so P and Q are disjoint and P union Q=J. Therefore the union of the X_ell over P together with their union over Q equals the union over J. This verifies the complementary-class construction as written. It does not identify the earlier R_{j,k} or (11)'s order-defined S_{j,k} with those two unions; that identification needs assumptions or definitions outside this isolated packet, and the literal starred/unstarred labels also differ.

scan060.N4: Targeted check of the two marginal NB cases, using the strict final inequality of (11). If j=k, no ell can satisfy j<=ell<j, so S_{j,j} is empty. If k is an immediate successor of j, the interval j<=ell<k consists only of j, so the displayed union is X_j. These checks need only the meaning of immediate successor in a partial order and the visible condition in (11); they do not require an order-reflecting map to the subsets X_i.

scan060.N5: The right-side union and intersection identities in (12) are retained as authorial assertions. In particular, R_{j,k} cap S_{j,k} is independent of the separate lower index i in (10), while the written right side is dotted X_i. This is a warning for the mathematics audit, not permission to replace the clear i by another index. No unconditional proof of these identities is claimed from the one-page packet.

scan060.N12: Cross-page check of (12): identifying the second displayed subset with (11)'s S is not automatic, since X_j contained in X_ell need not imply j<=ell in the permitted setup. Strict lower inclusions alone do not fix this. A finite discrete example has o<a,b<j,l<k with a,b incomparable and j,l incomparable, and pieces empty, {p}, {q}, {p,q}, {p,q,r}, {p,q,r,s}, respectively. Every strict comparison gives proper inclusion and (21d) holds, but R_{j,k}=S_{j,k}={p,q} while dotted X_k={p,q,r}; the second subset union also contains r. Thus both the second union identification and the displayed union equality fail in this allowed family. See N13 for a sufficient refinement.

scan060.N13: Refined union statement: read the two subsets by their written complementary predicates, retaining the starred/unstarred label mismatch in the transcription. The first union equals R_{j,k} by scan057 (3bis) for j<=k under (21d). If X_j contained in X_ell implies j<=ell (order reflection), the second predicate agrees with j<=ell<k in (11), so the second union is S_{j,k}, and the two unions give dotted X_k. The optional restriction to nonempty starred pieces on scan055 supplies order reflection by scan057.N13; it was not silently assumed for the unreduced family.

scan060.N14: The literal intersection equality ending in dotted X_i fails even in an order-reflecting chain with nonempty stars: I={0<1<2}, X_0={0}, X_1={0,1}, X_2={0,1,2}, with i=0,j=1,k=2, has R_{1,2} intersect S_{1,2}={0} while dotted X_0 is empty. Replacing i by j does not suffice for arbitrary k either. Take the Boolean poset of subsets of {a,b,c}, with X_A the discrete principal downset of A. For j={a}, k={a,b,c}, the point {b} lies in both R_{j,k} and S_{j,k}, but not in dotted X_j. This family has nonempty stars and satisfies (21d). See N15 for valid statements; the visible i is unchanged.

scan060.N15: A valid general identity is R_{j,k} intersect S_{j,k} = union over j<=ell<k of (R_j intersect X_ell), by distributing intersection and using X_ell contained in X_k. If k is an immediate successor of j, N4 gives S_{j,k}=X_j. Then, under the strict-inclusion hypothesis sufficient for scan057 (4), the intersection equals dotted X_j. This successor refinement does not claim the same simplification for general k.

scan060.N16: Targeted set-algebra check of (13), under the preferred S reading and the visible live R_{i,k} in (10): S_{k,k}=empty gives V_{i,k}^k=V_{i,k} from (5). The other extreme V_{i,k}^i=V_{i,k}^* follows when R_{i,k} union S_{i,k}=dotted X_k, for example under N13's order-reflection condition, since both then remove the same set from the barred neighbourhood. The diagonal equalities inherit scan058.N9's qualification. This does not prove existence or local triviality of the proposed tubular neighbourhoods or bundles.

scan060.N17: Exact finite-set verification of the three examples in N12/N14 is saved in scripts/check_scan060_counterexamples.py and audit/scan060_counterexample_certificate.json. The computation checks poset axioms, monotonicity, proper inclusion at strict comparisons, and every pairwise common-lower intersection: 36, 9 and 64 ordered pairs. It also computes the unions, intersections and starred nonemptiness used above. Discrete finite topology makes the listed finite cover closed and locally finite. This is a certificate for these explicit counterexamples, not a formal verification of a general theorem.

scan060.N18. Blind adjudication leaves five additional local doubts explicit: topos/topo, the abbreviated succ./success., the possible fused equality stroke on the negated containment relation, the low k/n in the lower R index of (12), and a small o-like loop after germes and its comma. The loop was omitted by both witnesses and is included without interpreting its role.
